newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end firm on hopes for economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end firm on hopes for economic growth.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed firm on Friday as investors believed the country showed signs of healthy economic growth that would lead to solid company profits, brokers said.
They said prices would likely rise again on Monday.

The General Index .IGRA climbed 0.24 percent to 1,548.1 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL rose 0.26 percent to 2,232.6 points. In 1,212 trades, volume was 33.2 million soles ($12.6 million), brokers said.
Players hunted for bargains and bought stocks they believed had lagged behind the previous two sessions' small rises.
"This month's rebound in cement output is making people believe Gross Domestic Production (GDP) will be good in January," Luis Cueva of local brokerage Argos said.
Peru's January cement output rose 10.9 percent to 341,735 tonnes compared with the same month last year, the private Association of Cement Producers (ASOCEM) said Thursday.
On the bolsa Friday, the country's largest cement company, Cementos Lima, closed up 0.67 percent at 4.50 soles on strong volume of 1.1 million shares.
Among other leaders, benchmark Telefonica climbed 0.17 percent, closing at 5.83 soles on volume of 2.3 million shares. Tin miner Minsur rose 0.21 percent to 9.40 soles on volume of 180,000 shares.
